Meet your clinician

Autumn Alexander

LMHCA

Licensed Mental Health Counselor Associate (LMHCA)

Autumn works with children (6+), teens, and adults navigating emotional and behavioral challenges, trauma-related concerns, and difficulties with emotional regulation. Her background also includes supporting families through intensive behavioral health services.

Ask about appointments with AutumnMeet the team

How this clinician describes their work

Autumn takes a relational, person-centered, and trauma-informed approach to therapy. Drawing from her experience in youth behavioral health, adult outpatient counseling, and intensive family support services, she emphasizes understanding each client's unique experiences, relationships, and cultural background. Her work focuses on creating a supportive, collaborative environment while helping clients develop practical skills to navigate emotional and behavioral challenges.

Who she works with

Children ages 6+, teens, young adults, and adults; experience supporting families.

Therapy for

Parenting and family stress

Support for families navigating children's behavioral and emotional challenges, strengthening communication, and developing practical strategies to support their child's well-being.

Emotional regulation

Support for understanding difficult emotions, developing coping strategies, and building skills to manage emotional responses in everyday life.

Behavioral challenges

Support for children and adolescents experiencing behavioral difficulties, with an emphasis on emotional awareness, coping skills, and positive behavioral strategies.

Trauma-related concerns

Trauma-informed support that emphasizes emotional safety, understanding difficult experiences, and developing healthy coping strategies.

Identity and cultural concerns

A supportive space to explore personal identity, cultural experiences, and the ways relationships and social environments influence emotional well-being.

Approaches

Person-centered therapy

A collaborative approach that emphasizes empathy, understanding, and each client's unique experiences, strengths, and personal goals.

Trauma-informed care

An approach that prioritizes emotional safety, trust, and understanding how difficult experiences can influence emotions, behaviors, and relationships.

Liberation psychology

An approach that considers how cultural identity, lived experiences, relationships, and broader social systems influence mental health and personal well-being.

Relational, integrative approach

An approach that considers the influence of relationships and personal experiences while drawing from different therapeutic perspectives to meet each client's individual needs.
